title: Rabbi Naftali Besser: Staying Inspired-  “Parashat Emor"
summary: Rabbi Besser discusses the laws and spiritual significance of the Korban Toda, explaining why it is brought and why it must be consumed within a limited timeframe. He connects this ancient practice to the modern custom of Birkhat Ha Gomel, emphasizing the requirement of a minyan for this public expression of gratitude. The class also touches upon the meaning of the Omer and the historical tragedy involving the students of Rabbi Akiba.
questions: Why must the Korban Toda be eaten within a shorter time than other peace offerings?
Why is the mitzva of Kiddush Hashem mentioned in the context of the Korban Toda?
Is a minyan required to say Birkhat Ha Gomel?
What is the meaning of the word Omer?
